Sara — thanks for the note and the doc. Forwarding to Marissa and Aditya to align commercial and infra details. High-level answers and a proposed schedule below.

Short answers up front:
- Yes — Redwood Private supports controlled monthly staging rotations without manual data copy. We use continuous replication + snapshot promotion for the warm-standby -> active transition.
- KMS behaviour: customer-managed keys (CMKs) are used per-region; we perform key policy sync and per-request wrapping. We do not replicate raw key material across regions — rather we orchestrate key access via customer KMS policies and an envelope wrapping model.
- Typical windows: 4–6 hour maintenance window for the first promoted rotation (includes validation + smoke tests), 1–2 hour window for subsequent routine rotations once warmed. RPO targets depend on replication frequency — we recommend max 5 minutes for transactional workloads.

Proposed staging rotation (high level):
1) Network preflight (24–48h): CIDR checks, BGP prep, peering verification, firewall rules.
2) ACL/KMS checks (3h): validate CMK policies, test key unwrap/wrap flows.
3) Snapshot & sync (1h): final incremental snapshot and verify replication offsets.
4) Promote warm-standby (4h window): cut traffic via routing change (BGP prep and DNS TTL drop), run smoke tests, monitor logs/metrics.
5) Rollback path (within same window): automated fallback if latency/smoke tests fail.

I've attached a quick calc for capacity and staging rotation runbook (staging-rotation-calc.xlsx).

Next steps: 1) Marissa to confirm contract/acceptance criteria and procurement point of contact; 2) Aditya to provide a preflight checklist and proposed dates for an initial run before 2028-06-30.

Thanks — adding technical detail for the preflight and a proposed concrete window. Quoting Sean below for context.

Minimum preflight checklist (must complete 48h before rotation):
- CIDR & subnet validation: ensure no overlaps; provide full IP ranges for peering and NAT.
- BGP prep: community tags for region-preference, failover AS-path prep, test route withdraws in a sandbox.
- VPC peering & routing: confirm route priorities and blackhole safeguards.
- Firewall rules: allow health checks and control-plane traffic between regions.
- KMS/CMK: validate key policy grants for the Redwood service account, run test wrap/unwrap flows against the standby key (do not export key material).
- Replication offsets: verify WAL lag (or equivalent) < 5 minutes for RPO compliance.
- Observability: ensure logs (s3/rsyslog) and traces are flowing to the audit bucket; enable short-term retention snapshot for the test.
- Smoke test suite: end-to-end requests, auth flows, and data access checks. Provide expected pass/fail thresholds up front.

Proposed first rotation window: 2028-07-11 02:00–08:00 UTC (which corresponds to local working windows in EU/APAC for minimal business impact). We recommend doing the run in a low-volume weekend slab; if this is acceptable, we will:
1) Run preflight on 2028-07-09–10;
2) Dry run routing-only test on 2028-07-10;
3) Full promote/promotion on 2028-07-11.

If you approve the window, we will produce the go/no-go checklist and a one-page evidence pack suitable for auditors. I attached the network-preflight-checklist.txt with the detailed commands and test IDs.
